title: pi-do-always configuration
description: Configuration for the /do-always Pi extension (https://github.com/aginies/pi-do-always). Either an array of tasks, or an object with `tasks` plus the global settings. Read from ~/.pi/agent/do-always.json (global) and <project>/.pi/do-always.json (project); the project file wins per task `name`, and its global settings win over the global file's. Unknown keys are ignored at runtime — this schema is deliberately stricter (`additionalProperties: false`) so a typo is caught in the editor instead of silently doing nothing.

taskList.description: The array form of the config: just the tasks.

configObject.description: The object form of the config: tasks plus global settings.

$schema.description: Editor hint pointing at this schema. Ignored at runtime.

shortcut.description: Key that opens the task selector, e.g. "f4" or "ctrl+shift+p" (Pi key-id syntax). null disables the shortcut. Default "f4". The project file's value wins.

merge.description: How project tasks combine with the global ones: "override" (default) replaces a global task with the same name; "append" keeps the global tasks and only adds new project task names. The project file's value wins.

report.description: Whether chain runs write a Markdown report file in the project root. The project file's value wins.

questionnaire.description: Whether a completed run whose reply carries a plan block offers the selection questionnaire. false keeps the plain summary notification (and no plan block is asked for). The project file's value wins.

hidePlan.description: Whether the raw plan block is stripped from the transcript after a completed run (TUI only; non-TUI modes always keep it). The project file's value wins.

planNudge.description: Whether a completed plan-mode run whose reply has no usable plan block triggers one follow-up asking the agent to emit it. The project file's value wins.

anyPlan.description: Whether an ordinary turn (no auto-run armed) whose reply ENDS with a parseable plan block is captured, stripped and offered as an "Ad-hoc plan" proposal. The project file's value wins.

markers.description: Glyph set for the UI's markers: the run-mode markers, the cursor, the chain widget's step markers, the questionnaire's tier/item marks, the rules and the footer key hints. Use "ascii" when the terminal or font lacks the unicode glyphs (or renders them double-width). Prose punctuation in notifications and reports is unaffected. The project file's value wins.

aliases.description: Global alias map: short name → task name, e.g. { "rc": "Review changes" }. Case-insensitive, tried before the task's own name. The project file's value wins.

chains.description: Saved chains: chain name → task names in execution order, run with `/do-always chain <name>` and listed by `/do-always chain`. Steps resolve by task name or alias. The project file's chain wins over the global one with the same name.

chainSteps.description: A saved chain's steps: task names (or aliases) in execution order, at most 8. Repeated names are dropped at load time.

task.description: One task: a prompt the selector can fill into the editor or send.

name.description: Short unique id, used for `/do-always <name>`. A project task replaces the global task with the same name.

prompt.description: The text filled into the editor (or sent). Supports {{placeholders}} — cwd, date, branch, last_commit, files_changed, files_changed_count, user, diff_stat, repo, staged_files, unstaged_files, selected_commits. May be empty only together with "autoRun": true.

description.description: One-line label shown next to the task in the selector.

category.description: Group header the task is shown under (e.g. "Plan", "Do", "Docs", "Ops"). Matching is case-insensitive; tasks without one fall under "Other". The "Plan" category also implies plan mode unless `mode`/`autoRun`/`questionnaire` say otherwise.

aliases.description: Short names that also resolve to this task on the command line. Case-insensitive, tried before the task's own name.

mode.description: How the task runs when selected: "plan" sends the prompt with the plan-block instruction and offers the questionnaire on the reply; "run" sends it as-is (plain summary notification); "fill" puts it in the editor. Wins over `autoRun` and `questionnaire`. ctrl+p in the selector, or `/do-always mode <task>`, overrides it for the session.

autoRun.description: Legacy spelling of part of `mode`: true sends the prompt on selection instead of filling the editor. When omitted, "Plan"-category tasks auto-run and everything else fills. Ignored when `mode` is set.

questionnaire.description: Legacy spelling of part of `mode`: whether this task's completed run offers the plan questionnaire. false keeps the plain summary and stops the plan block being requested at all. Ignored when `mode` is set.

hidePlan.description: Whether the raw plan block is stripped from this task's finalized reply in the TUI (the questionnaire still reads the captured text).

browser.description: Open a browser on selection instead of injecting the prompt. "commits" opens the date-grouped commit browser; the selection then drives the task (directly when the prompt uses {{selected_commits}}, otherwise via a picker of Plan tasks).

hidden.description: Hide the task from the selector and the list commands. It can still be run by name and is offered by the commit picker.

notForCommits.description: Exclude the task from the commit picker ("run on the selected commits") because it does not operate on a set of commits. Everything else is unaffected.

requireDirty.description: Legacy guard: block the task when the working tree is clean. Equivalent to { "type": "requireDirty" } in `guards`, and combined with any entries there.

guards.description: Selection-time guards: each one blocks the task with a message (it is not hidden) when its condition is unmet.

guard.description: A selection-time guard. Every guard except requireDirty needs a string `value`.

type.description: requireDirty: changed files exist. requireBranch: the current branch equals `value`. requireRepo: the git-remote basename equals `value`. requireFilePattern: a changed file matches the glob `value` (`*` within a segment, `**` across, `?` one character).

value.description: Required for requireBranch, requireRepo and requireFilePattern; ignored for requireDirty.

when.description: Environment condition controlling whether the task is shown in the selector and lists (and refused when picked by name). The string form is a single condition; the object form is a set of conditions that must all hold (logical AND).

git.description: Inside a git work tree (true) or not (false).

branch.description: The current branch equals this name (exact match).

file.description: A path that must exist in the working tree (must stay under the project root).

repo.description: Equals the git-remote basename context value.
